title: Transfer of product from road tanker to storage tank TK-101
summary: Line up, start and monitor a 55 m3 flammable liquid transfer from a road tanker into an atmospheric storage tank whose freeboard at the end of the batch is 0.74 m.

warnings.label: Step 8 makes the vent confirmation conditional on doubt, and the cue for doubt is a roof camera in another building
Step 12 assigns a 30 minute monitoring task with no watch rotation and no instruction on what to do if the operator has to leave
V1, V2 and V3 are identical handwheels on one manifold with no positive position indication
The procedure requires the isolation register to be obtained, not reconciled line by line against the permit
No stated maximum elapsed time for the transfer, so a stalled line-up can be watched indefinitely
The only barrier against continued filling after the pump stops is a phone call to the control room

steps.title: Confirm a valid transfer permit for the tank on the dispatch note
steps.text: Hold a valid transfer permit for the tank named on the dispatch note.

errors.text: Permit signed in the office against yesterday's load; the tank named on it is TK-103
Dispatch note and permit agree on product but name different tanks. The operator matches on product, not on tank
No permit at all, because it is the fourth load of the week into the same tank

steps.title: Reconcile the instrument isolation register against the permit
steps.text: If the tank has had instrument work in the last 14 days, obtain the isolation register from the control room and confirm that LT-101 and LSHH-101 have been returned to service and signed back by the instrument fitter.

errors.text: The register is in the control room and the shift is behind. Assumed the fitter signed it back like he always does
Confirmed the row for LT-101. The isolation that matters is the next row down, LSHH-101
Transmitter confirmed in service. Nobody looked at whether the high-high switch loop was proved after the bench test

steps.title: Confirm the vehicle is bonded, earthed and the hose made up
steps.text: Confirm that the vehicle is bonded and earthed and that the hose is made up with the correct couplings and the break-away arm in service.

errors.text: Bond clip is on the painted chassis rail. It looks connected and measures nothing
Walked past it because the driver said he had just made up for the last load
Checked the bond on the vehicle in the adjacent bay

steps.title: Open the tank inlet valve V1
steps.text: Open the tank inlet valve V1 on TK-101.

errors.text: Opened V2, the draw-off valve on the same manifold with the same handwheel and a tag nobody can read from the working platform
Assumed V1 had been left open from the last transfer into this tank
Cracked the cross-connect V3 open to free a stuck stem, and left it there
Rising stem valve turned the wrong way: the handwheel came up, which reads as open

steps.title: Confirm the tank draw-off valve V2 is closed
steps.text: Confirm the tank draw-off valve V2 is closed.

errors.text: Knew V2 was closed because he closed it himself at the end of the last transfer
The valve is quarter-turn and the indicator plate was refitted upside down after the packing change

steps.title: Confirm the cross-connect valve V3 to TK-102 is closed
steps.text: Confirm the cross-connect valve V3 to TK-102 is closed.

errors.text: Closed by hand but the stem packing is stiff and the disc is two turns off its seat
V3 is only used for tank cleaning, so it never occurs to him as something to check

steps.title: Walk the line from the tanker to the tank
steps.text: Walk the line from the tanker to the tank and confirm every valve is in the position stated above.

errors.text: Did the walk from the rack only as far as the first bend, where the manifold is out of sight
Confirmed the valves visible from the walkway, which does not include the tank bottom outlet
Walked the line while talking on the radio about the next load, and registered the positions he expected rather than the ones he passed

steps.title: Confirm the tank vent valve V4 is open
steps.text: Confirm the tank vent valve V4 is open. The vent line was isolated for the roof inspection work; if in doubt, ask the control room to confirm on the roof camera.

errors.text: The vent was shut for the roof inspection. It is up the platform ladder, off the transfer walk, and nobody thought of it
Opened the nitrogen blanket valve next to the vent. The tank now pressurises instead of breathing, which looks like a healthy result on the status board
Climbed the ladder, found the handle stiff, forced it a quarter turn and assumed it was through

steps.title: Check the hose and clear the drip tray
steps.text: Open the hose box, check the hose for damage and confirm the drip tray is clear.

errors.text: Cleared the tray by pushing last shift's standing liquid over the weep hole into the bund drain, so the tray is empty for this transfer and the bund is not
Tray looked dry from above

steps.title: Start pump P-201
steps.text: Start pump P-201 and confirm flow is heard at the tank inlet.

errors.text: Local handle left in hand after the last job, so the start from the control room does nothing
Started P-202, the pump for the other rack, because the panel tag moved when the panel was replaced
Started the pump with the inlet still shut, which is the definition of a dead-headed line

steps.title: Record the start level on the permit
steps.text: Record the start level from the local indicator on TK-101 on the permit.

errors.text: Read the gauge board of the tank two bays along, which sits at a similar height
No start level written down, so the delivered quantity has to be judged by eye later

steps.title: Watch the level and stop the pump at 9.30 m
steps.text: The transfer takes approximately 30 minutes. Go back to the rack and watch the level indicator. Stop the pump when the level reaches 9.30 m.

errors.text: Went back to the rack office to close the permit paperwork, and the level crossed while he was typing
The local indicator has been reading low since the transmitter bench test. He stops the pump when it says 9.30 and the tank is already above it
Left the watch entirely to help the other bay discharge a late load
Level rising slower than the estimate, so he opened the recirculation bypass to keep the pump loaded, against step 13

steps.title: Stop the pump when the meter reads 55 m3
steps.text: Stop pump P-201 when the meter on the rack reads 55 m3.

errors.text: The totaliser on the adjacent rack is at a similar number and is the one visible from the road
The meter is a cumulative total, not a batch total. He works the difference out from memory
Already stopped on level, so he does not look at the meter again

steps.title: Close V1 and isolate the pump
steps.text: Close the tank inlet valve V1. Stop and isolate the pump at the local handle.

errors.text: Closed V1 before stopping the pump, so the trapped column hammered and the couplings wept
Pump stopped at the handle but not isolated. The next crew will find it running against a closed inlet
Closed V3 instead of V1, leaving the inlet open to a tank that is no longer receiving

steps.title: Drain and disconnect the hose
steps.text: Drain and disconnect the hose into the drip tray. Return the hose to the hose box and hang the not-in-service tag on the vehicle stand.

errors.text: Broke the coupling before the line had drained, so the contents of the hose went on the deck
Left the hose in the tray, dripping

steps.title: Complete the log and update the status board
steps.text: Enter the delivered quantity, the finish level and your initials on the tank log. Update the tank status board.

errors.text: Written up next shift from memory, so a wrong-tank receipt stays invisible until the monthly stock reconciliation
Logged the indicated level as the true level, carrying the instrument error into the stock record
Status board left showing TK-101 as not receiving, so the next dispatch is planned into a full tank

steps.title: Emergency: stop on a release
steps.text: If product is released on the rack deck, stop the pump immediately from the rack emergency stop, close V1 if you can reach it safely, and call the control room on channel 1.

errors.text: Release not noticed, or noticed and not believed
